text.en: In 1973 villagers in Chamoli hugged trees to stop them being cut. Their movement, Chipko, saved forests and inspired the world.

Natural resources are renewable (forests, crops, wind, solar) or non-renewable (coal, petroleum, minerals); conservation is their proper use and management.
Forests provide wood, food, fodder, fibre and medicine, act as carbon sinks, regulate climate, increase rainfall, prevent floods and landslides.
Deforestation (agriculture, urbanization, dams, roads, fires) causes floods, drought, soil erosion, species loss and desertification; India loses about 1.5 million hectares a year.
Conservation measures: afforestation (Van Mahotsav), social forestry, National Forest Policy (1952, 1988) and the Forest Conservation Act 1980.
The Chipko movement of 1973 in Chamoli protected trees and won a 15 year ban on tree felling in Himalayan forests in 1980.
Wildlife Protection Act 1972 prohibits hunting, creates sanctuaries and national parks and regulates trade in wild animal products.
Jim Corbett National Park (1936) was the first in India; there are 15 biosphere reserves, and the Nilgiris is one in Tamil Nadu.
Initiatives: Project Tiger (1973), Project Elephant (1992), Crocodile project (1976) and Sea Turtle project (1999); bodies include IUCN, WWF and BNHS.

problem.en: How does deforestation lead to floods and drought?

text.en: Trees hold soil and slow rainwater.
Without trees, rain runs off quickly causing floods and erosion.
Less transpiration reduces rainfall, and groundwater falls, causing drought.

points.en: Forests and wildlife are linked and need conservation.
